items.heading: Amendment A1 (20 October 2026): Resend-only sign-in, consent, webhooks and test isolation
items.text: **Amendment status: PROPOSED_AMENDMENT, PENDING_OWNER_APPROVAL.** The owner's decisions of 20 October 2026 are recorded here as owner-supplied decisions (CONFIRMED_OWNER_CONFIGURATION). Changes to D1 to D14 are owner-only (Engineering Standards section 11), so this amendment is not applied as an activated change until the owner records approval in the repository. Historical text of D11 and the earlier launch rows is kept and marked superseded. Only D11 changes; D1 to D10 and D12 to D14 are unchanged.

items.heading: A1.1 Supersession of D11
items.text: - **Superseded:** D11 "second email provider for sign-in fallback" (section 1, section 4.1 fallback, section 6 failover, section 12 second-provider dependency, section 13 outage gate, go/no-go items 2 and 3, Goal Stage B and blocker list).

items.heading: A1.1 Supersession of D11
items.text: - **Current policy (D11-R):** production sign-in OTP is delivered by Resend only. No SMTP route and no automatic second-provider routing exist for sign-in OTP. A missing or invalid Resend configuration produces a controlled sign-in unavailability state. Existing sessions are not invalidated by a provider outage.

items.heading: A1.1 Supersession of D11
items.text: - Other email workflows (notifications, outreach) keep their own provider setting, which is audited separately before any change. SMTP is not removed globally.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Six-digit code from a cryptographically secure random source; five-minute validity; single use; HMAC digest storage with a secret separate from the Resend API key; no plaintext OTP stored or logged.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Sixty-second resend cooldown; a new code replaces the previous one; duplicate sends prevented under concurrency and retry.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Five incorrect attempts per verification window, then lockout with backoff (section 4.1). Rate limits per email and per IP, shared across instances through Redis.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Atomic verification and consumption; constant-time comparison; expired, used and replaced codes rejected; one session per challenge; secure cookies; CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated mutations.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Account enumeration resistance: existing, new and disabled accounts get the same status, body, structure, cooldown and rate-limit responses. Provider failures return the same generic unavailable response.

items.heading: A1.2 Sign-in OTP standard
items.text: - Recovery and email-change rules in section 4.1 are unchanged.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 1. Missing Resend key: sign-in unavailable; startup or runtime check fails closed; no fallback route used.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 2. Invalid Resend key: controlled failure; key never shown in logs or responses.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 3. Provider outage: new sign-ins show "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable"; existing sessions keep working.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 4. Provider timeout: bounded timeout; no second send; user sees the same unavailable state.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 5. Provider retry behaviour: bounded retries with an idempotency key per challenge; no duplicate valid codes.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 6. Controlled sign-in unavailability: request logged with request ID and rejected, never silently dropped.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 7. Existing-session continuity during the outage.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 8. Recovery after Resend service restoration: the state clears and sign-in succeeds with a new code.

items.heading: A1.3 Required Resend failure tests (replace the fallback-provider tests)
items.text: 9. No silent SMTP or secondary-provider routing (negative test on the send path).

items.heading: A1.4 OTP and queued messages
items.text: - Sign-in OTP messages are not queued for later delivery, because a delayed code is misleading and may already be expired. They fail fast and show the unavailable state.

items.heading: A2.3 Gateway requirements
items.text: - Model identifiers come from an explicit allowlist. Routing considers capability, latency, reliability, privacy, and cost, within policy.

items.heading: A2.3 Gateway requirements
items.text: - Controlled fallback between approved models only where the data-handling terms permit. Fallback never bypasses quotas or spend ceilings.

items.heading: A2.3 Gateway requirements

items.heading: A2.3 Gateway requirements
items.text: - Streaming where appropriate, with cancellation and usage accounting. Usage records include tokens, estimated provider cost, error category, and latency. Prompt content is not logged.

items.heading: A2.3 Gateway requirements

items.heading: A2.4 Privacy and data handling
items.text: - Send only the minimum data a feature needs (section 9). No private contact details unless the feature requires them.

items.heading: A2.4 Privacy and data handling
items.text: - No training on user or portal content without explicit opt-in (section 9). Review and record OpenRouter routing, privacy terms, and retention settings before any production user data is sent. items.heading: A2.5 Testing
items.text: Automated tests use mocked OpenRouter responses by default. A mocked request does not prove live inference. The required AI tests are: server-side key protection; allowlist enforcement; authorization and tenant isolation; token and spend limits; concurrency limits; provider errors; timeouts and retries; streaming cancellation; fallback rules; usage accounting; prompt-injection defense; sensitive-data redaction; malformed responses; outage recovery; and a guard against accidental real calls in CI. items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB1 | Real login and logout | Sign-in by Resend email OTP creates a server-side session. Logout revokes that session on the server. Sign out everywhere revokes all sessions. Idle and absolute expiry are enforced. | E2E @critical: sign in, reach a protected page, log out; back navigation and direct URLs return to sign-in. Integration: a revoked session token is rejected server-side. Sign-out-everywhere test with two sessions. | PLANNED |

The earlier conditional password-reset wording is superseded and kept only for traceability in the owner update of 20 October 2026. | Route scan: no password-set or password-reset endpoint or form exists in the build; recovery uses only the email OTP flow (integration test). | NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_REASON (Resend-only email OTP; no password credential) |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB3 | Email verification | Email is verified by a Resend OTP at sign-up and on every email change. An email change needs an OTP sent to the old address and one sent to the new address. Unverified accounts cannot reach protected areas. | Integration: unverified account blocked from protected routes; expired and reused OTP rejected; email change without both OTPs rejected; OTP sent only through this product's Resend account. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB4 | Loading states | Every asynchronous action (sign-in, saves, uploads, AI or provider calls, bookings, pagination) shows loading feedback, a timeout path with retry, a slow-network state and duplicate-submit protection. | Playwright @critical under a throttled slow-network profile: each async action shows loading, times out to a recoverable message, and a double click sends one request. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB5 | Empty states | Every list or screen with no data explains the situation and offers one next action. No sample, invented or placeholder statistics. | Component and E2E: a fresh account renders each empty state with its action; a text scan finds no invented figures or placeholder text. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB6 | Clear error messages | User-facing errors are plain and actionable, announced to screen readers, and carry a request ID for support. Technical detail goes only to protected diagnostics. | Integration: forced 500, timeout and validation errors return non-technical text, a request ID, and no stack trace or internal path. axe check confirms the error sits in a live region. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB7 | Form validation | One validation schema runs on client and server. Errors are linked to their fields and summarized. Entered input is kept after an error. The server rejects input that bypasses client checks. | Unit: shared schema cases (valid, invalid, empty, too long, special characters, each launch language). E2E: an error keeps the entered input. API: a request that bypasses client checks returns 422 with field errors. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB8 | Rate limiting | Server-side limits per email, account and IP on sign-in, OTP requests and protected actions. Limits are shared across instances; a Redis or limiter outage fails protected surfaces closed. Proxy headers and concurrent requests cannot bypass them. | Integration: N+1 OTP requests in the window return 429 with Retry-After; two app instances share one counter; rotating X-Forwarded-For does not reset the limit; a forced limiter outage fails sign-in closed while health stays reachable. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB9 | Database backups | Encrypted automated backups of each product database, with an off-host copy and an immutable or object-locked copy where the host supports it. A backup counts as operational only after a verified restore. | Scheduled restore drill: the latest backup is restored to a disposable database; row counts and checksums match the source snapshot; result recorded. A failed backup job raises an alert. | PLANNED |

items.heading: B. The 19 launch baseline controls
items.text: | LB10 | Row level security | PostgreSQL row level security on user-owned records, with dedicated least-privilege application roles. RLS is defence in depth; application authorization checks still apply. | Integration: as the application role, a query for another account's records returns zero rows; direct SQL against another tenant is denied; the authorization matrix passes with RLS disabled, proving application checks work independently. | PLANNED |

A request for a production source map returns 404. | PLANNED |
